body.statement: Determine \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\) up to constants depending only on \(\beta,D\) for every joint sequence \(n\to\infty\), even \(m=m_n\ge2\), and \(0<\tau_n\le1/(8n)\). The answer must identify every unavoidable logarithmic factor, give a necessary-and-sufficient joint-sequence criterion for \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\), construct a computable \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{tail}}\) attaining the frontier, and prove a same-class lower bound against \(\mathfrak A_{n,m}\) that remains sharp through sparse-dominance, collective-contribution, and local-to-tied regimes. Express the answer as strict comparisons with both named baselines. In the dense reallocating regime \(m\to\infty\), \(m\log(2m)=o(n)\), and \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\to0\), identify the maximal subregimes on which capacity averaging gives \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)=o\{\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\}\) and the complementary subregimes on which the coordinatewise bound is unavoidable. Across every vanishing-regret regime, quantify the separation from \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}(n,m)\) rather than importing a regular-policy penalty.
body.justification: The distribution of missed heavy cells after optimal capacity reallocation, rather than coordinatewise estimation error, is the new decision-theoretic object.
body.gap: The probability display in Theorem 3 of CarpentierKim2015 supplies an adaptive single-tail upper rate and Theorem 4 supplies its adaptive lower bound with the log-log loss. After the proposal's separate translation \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\), these results motivate the coordinatewise benchmark but do not state which dense capacity-mixture regimes strictly remove its familywise penalty; AtheyWager2021 likewise does not explain the separation from regular welfare regret.
body.consumer: The result gives the model-based extrapolation boundary at which the upper-cost policy objective of OsamaZachariahStoica2020 becomes statistically actionable rather than uninformative.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine the distribution, under the product paired-splice prior and an unrestricted capacity-constrained learner, of the number \(H\) of missed heavy cells at testing information from order one through order \(\log m\), and match the resulting exact expected log-sum-exp loss by a full-class learner without coordinatewise familywise localization.
obligation.obstruction: Assouad's argument proves only \(\mathbb E H\gtrsim m\) at constant neighboring information. For larger information, the loss is concave and nonlinear in \(H\), so neither a mean Hamming-error lower bound nor Jensen's inequality supplies the required lower bound. Capacity reallocation can correlate errors across pairs, while a coordinatewise upper proof pays \((\log m)^{\varkappa}\). The frozen primitives contain no distributional ambiguity lemma closing this gap.
obligation.attempted: I derived the exact missed-cell regret equation, checked same-class Hall membership and neighboring product divergence, expanded the fixed-information Assouad bound, and proved the coordinatewise thresholded upper bound. I also tested the sparse-error route against the capacity projection inequality; it controls the mean at constant information but does not control the rare-event law needed when \(\delta\ell\) is large.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved uniform bracket is
\[
c_{\beta,D}\ell\min\{1,(m/n)^\varkappa\}
\leq\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\leq C_{\beta,D}\ell\min\{1,[m\log(2m)/n]^\varkappa\}.
\]
For the paired splice at an arbitrary testing amplitude \(\delta\), if \(H\) heavy controls are missed then the exact regret \(h\) satisfies
\[
4h=\log\left[1+\frac Hm\{e^{\delta(b+h)}-1\}\right].
\]
Neighbor information is of order \(N\delta^{2+4/\beta}\).  Thus the unresolved step is distributional control of \(H\), not the Hall modulus or the capacity algebra.
